verdict.headline: Nvidia's blowout quarter gives the AI trade a green light heading into Jackson Hole
verdict.rationale_short: NVDA simultaneously cleared both bars of the dual-bar test: gross margin at 75% (above 74.9% threshold) and Q3 guidance of $108B versus $104.2B consensus, with data-center revenue of $89B up 117% year over year. Revenue of $96.2B beat the $92.2B consensus by $4B; EPS of $2.22 beat $2.09. The AWS announcement — 2 million Nvidia GPU units purchased, Vera CPU integrated with the Rubin architecture — is the largest single hyperscaler commitment disclosed this cycle and directly refutes the OpenAI 'Jalapeno' custom-chip competitive thesis that had overhung the complex entering the print. CFO Colette Kress guided FY28 revenue growth of approximately 70% and CPU revenue more than doubling, extending visibility well beyond the current fiscal year. The macro backdrop is unambiguously constructive: Brent at $86.93 (-1.03%) posts a fourth consecutive session decline from Monday's $93.09, now $7.07 below the $94 regime trigger; the 10Y at 4.64% (-8bps) and the 30Y at approximately 5.19% both declined as July core PCE printed exactly in-line at 3.3% — the in-line read drew a line under the bond-market anxiety from last week's yield spike. Headline PCE at 3.7% was 0.1pp above the Dow Jones consensus but attributable to energy and food pass-through rather than services re-acceleration; the market correctly read this as non-threatening to the September FOMC calculus. Both regime indicators (Brent and 30Y) are retreating from their respective triggers simultaneously. The single remaining gate: Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote tomorrow (Friday, August 28) at 10 AM ET, 19 days before the September 16 FOMC. Markets are pricing 33% odds of a September hike and 69% of fund managers expect a neutral Warsh tone — neutral is priced in. Goldman Sachs warned of amplified FX volatility around the keynote given the unresolved 3-way dissent from July 29 FOMC (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan voted for a hike — the first such 3-way split since 2016). If Warsh is neutral or dovish, horizon extends to 1-2 weeks. Tonight's AH event: MRVL reports, providing the first independent test of whether the hyperscaler AI infrastructure demand NVDA cited is sector-wide or company-specific.

bear_case: The constructive setup is real but contains two time-bombs. First, and most proximate: Kevin Warsh steps to the Jackson Hole podium tomorrow morning (Friday, August 28, 10 AM ET) with a 3-way dissent from July's FOMC in his pocket, headline PCE at 3.7%, and core at 3.3% — both above the 2% target. If Warsh frames the speech around the headline PCE reading rather than labor market weakness (-23,000 July payrolls), September FOMC hike odds could reprice from 33% to 45-50% in minutes. That repricing would push the 30Y back through the 5.30% regime trigger — re-activating the bear regime on the day after the most bullish NVDA print in years. Goldman Sachs has explicitly flagged amplified FX volatility for the EUR/USD pair, meaning the dislocation could spread to currency markets and create cross-asset feedback into equities. The 11bps cushion between current 30Y levels (~5.19%) and the trigger (~5.30%) sounds comfortable; a 15bps yield spike is less than an hour's work in a hawkish Fed repricing. Second, and more structural: OpenAI's 'Jalapeno' custom inference processor is entering the field in a compute environment where inference is displacing training as the dominant workload. If custom silicon captures 10-15% of the inference market by mid-2027, NVDA's FY28 guidance (+70% revenue growth) faces execution risk at the margin. The AWS commitment of 2M GPUs speaks to training and dense-compute demand; inference economics favor efficiency over raw power, which is exactly the attack surface custom chips optimize for. The bear case is not that NVDA failed — they cleared the dual bar with material margin — but that the re-risk is being built on the foundation of a Warsh keynote the market hasn't seen, over an inference market transition NVDA's guidance visibility doesn't fully extend to.
